newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait court sets date for U.S. wrestler hearing.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait court sets date for U.S. wrestler hearing.

text.p: A court on Tuesday lifted a travel ban and set a hearing for next month for a U.S. wrestler accused of assaulting a Kuwaiti television presenter when visiting the Gulf Arab state.
"The criminal court has lifted the travel ban imposed on the defendant and scheduled a hearing on May 13," said a legal source.

World Wrestling Federation (WWF) wrestler Leon White, known as Vader, on April 12 allegedly attacked Kuwaiti presenter Bassam al-Othman during a live interview when asked if his wrestling was fake, several viewers said.
White allegedly wrenched Othman's tie and used foul language to express dissatisfaction with the question on air during the Good Morning Kuwait show hosted by Othman on state television.
The court lifted the ban after receiving a certified guarantee from a Kuwaiti citizen that Leon White would appear in court when requested, the legal source said.
Othman, who has filed a law suit against White, wants a public apology and compensation of 120,000 dinars ($395,000), sources said.
If found guilty White, 38, could face a one-year jail term and a fine, lawyers said.
White of Boulder, Colorado, a football player turned wrestler, played with the Los Angeles Rams before joining the WWF in 1996.
A source close to the case said White had missed some WWF events due to the travel ban.
White was in Kuwait for a match with fellow a WWF wrestler known as Mankind.
